To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
investor overreaction to news about market-wide fundamentals is negatively correlated with cross-sectional dispersion of stock valuations and positively correlated with expected stock returns.
investor overreaction to a market-wide event is associated with a subsequent reduction in the cross-sectional dispersion of stock valuations.

investor overreaction to news is larger in periods when firm valuations in aggregate become more dispersed and that this leads to higher subsequent returns for stocks with less dispersion of firm valutations and lower returns for stocks with more dispersion of firm valutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of firm-level valuation dispersion in explaining expected stock returns.
the implications of the market-wide mispricing of stocks for firm-level misvaluation.
understanding the cross-section of expected stock returns and the role of investor overreaction in this cross section.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
investor overreaction to public information is a key factor that drives the cross-sectional dispersion of stock valuations, and that this dispersion is negatively related to future stock returns.
the dispersion of firm valuation is a good predictor of expected stock return.
the dispersion of firm valuation is negatively related to subsequent stock returns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cross section of stock returns is related to the dispersion of firm valuation and that dispersion in turn is related to investor overreaction to news.
the cross-section of firm valuation dispersion contains information about expected returns, and that this relationship is stronger for sets of stocks that are more likely to be mispriced.
the cross-section of expected returns depends on investor overreaction and arbitrage limits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
investor overreaction to common information is a source of cross-sectional dispersion in firm valuations, which in turn is a source of expected stock returns.
firm valuation dispersion can be a useful predictor of expected returns, especially in periods when investor overreaction is high.
investor overreaction to news about the economy can have a significant influence on the dispersion of firm valuation and expected stock returns.
